q-92180.name: Question 1
q-92180.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14130839/assets/f0faa033ca75ef5ea9b931ea4158ac735405686beb2befb03042381d7a15695e.png)

What multiplication problem is represented by the model above?
q-92180.worked_solution:
We have $\frac{3}{4}$ on the left and $\frac{12}{20}$ on the right.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14130839/assets/45b3351533a3b0d1fb0e9249d5f334ae06d65a5b8d544d5a796911b1dad64a39.png)

Therefore, the multiplication problem shown is:

$$
\frac{3}{4}\times \frac{4}{5}=\frac{12}{20}
$$
